fields.description:
## Context
Cut the next fix release, 0.13.1, from reviewed main using docs/releasing.md. Prior
package/tag: 0.13.0/v0.13.0 (currently live on PyPI and the latest GitHub Release). Only
6 commits landed on main since v0.13.0, all internal/non-user-facing (config/plan_review
split, SSM secret handling, MCP registry description-length fix, LLM cache/enrichment
tweaks) -- CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section on origin/main is empty, so step 1a is a
no-op retitle/placeholder rather than a curated entry. PyPI is immutable; publication uses
the dispatch-from-main workflow and its pypi environment approval.

Known risk carried from the prior release: ticket hyperbolic-pernicious-drongo (0.13.0)
closed FAILED because, after PyPI publish succeeded in one release.yml run, the mcp_registry
job failed (server.json description length), and by the time the fix landed, PyPI 0.13.0 was
already immutable so the workflow could not be re-dispatched (400 File already exists), and
the documented manual mcp-publisher fallback was blocked by a navapbc org OAuth-App
third-party-access restriction requiring org-admin action. The registry today still reports
0.12.0 as isLatest (0.13.0 never landed there). Mitigation for this release: before
dispatching, confirm the navapbc org OAuth-App access restriction has been resolved (or
obtain org-admin confirmation) so the documented manual mcp-publisher fallback is usable if
the in-run mcp_registry job fails again after PyPI publish succeeds. If mcp_registry still
cannot be made to report 0.13.1 after exhausting the automated job and the manual fallback,
this release closes with that single acceptance criterion explicitly marked
[non-codebase, known-blocked] with a linked follow-up ticket, rather than blocking the
already-published PyPI/GitHub Release channels indefinitely -- PyPI/GitHub Release do not get
yanked for a registry-only gap, since yank+patch does not fix a registry publish gap.

## Plan
- Fresh worktree from origin/main (../release-0.13.1); confirm prerequisites, identity,
  Gerrit rights, channel state, and the navapbc OAuth-App access posture (mitigation above).
- Bump pyproject.toml + every server.json version to 0.13.1; regenerate uv.lock; add a
  0.13.1 CHANGELOG section (today's date) using the "make changelog" tool as a starting
  point (curate its output if any conventional commits are picked up, otherwise write a
  minimal maintenance-release entry), with a fresh empty Unreleased section above it and
  updated compare links.
- Regenerate tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json (the __version__ bump), a required release
  step documented on the 0.13.0 release ticket.
- Preflight: version-lockstep guard, release-specific tests, lint, typecheck, full test
  suite, build, and a twine check of the built artifacts.
- Commit with DCO + Change-Id + rebar-ticket trailer; push to Gerrit; earn LLM-Review +1 and
  Verified +1 with no unresolved comments; Submit.
- Dispatch release.yml from main with version=0.13.1; approve the pypi environment
  deployment; monitor to a terminal result, watching the mcp_registry job specifically given
  the prior release's unresolved failure there.
- Verify PyPI and its PEP 740 provenance, the GitHub tag/release and artifacts, MCP Registry
  (confirm 0.13.1 isLatest), and the Homebrew tap bump (trigger autobump if needed).
- Channel-install nava-rebar with the mcp extra at 0.13.1 and run the packaged
  post-publication probe script.
- Record receipts on this ticket; close only after all acceptance criteria are met (or the
  single documented registry exception above, if it applies).

## File impact
- pyproject.toml -- package version bump
- server.json -- MCP manifest/package version bump
- uv.lock -- root package version lockstep with pyproject.toml
- CHANGELOG.md -- new 0.13.1 release section and compare links
- tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json -- __version__ bump

## Rollback / failure policy
Before publish: stop on any failed guard/review/CI vote; remediate via a new Gerrit
patchset. After publish, PyPI cannot be replaced: yank 0.13.1, de-list its GitHub Release,
and cut a fixed next patch version; never overwrite artifacts or retag published content.
If PyPI/GitHub Release publish succeeds but mcp_registry fails and the manual fallback is
also blocked (the exact 0.13.0 failure mode): do not yank the already-live PyPI/GitHub
Release artifacts for this reason alone; record the gap as a documented, linked follow-up
and mark the corresponding acceptance criterion [non-codebase, known-blocked] rather than
leaving the ticket in limbo.

## Testing
- Run the version-lockstep release guard script against pyproject.toml and server.json with
  version 0.13.1 and confirm it exits 0.
- Run "make lint", "make typecheck", and "make test" under the worktree virtualenv and
  confirm each exits 0.
- Run "python -m build" to produce the 0.13.1 wheel and sdist, then "python -m twine check"
  against the built artifacts and confirm it exits 0.
- Run the pypi-attestations verifier against the published 0.13.1 wheel, scoped to the
  navapbc/rebar repository, and confirm it exits 0.
- Install the channel-published nava-rebar[mcp]==0.13.1 build and run the packaged
  scripts/probe_rebar.py probe against it, confirming zero failures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] pyproject.toml declares version 0.13.1.
- [ ] server.json top-level version is 0.13.1.
- [ ] Every server.json packages[].version is 0.13.1.
- [ ] uv.lock records the root nava-rebar package at version 0.13.1.
- [ ] Running "uv lock --check" exits 0.
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md contains a 0.13.1 section dated with today's release date.
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md has a fresh Unreleased section and correct 0.13.1 compare links.
- [ ] tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json reflects __version__ 0.13.1.
- [ ] The release_guards.py version-lockstep check exits 0 for version 0.13.1 against
      pyproject.toml and server.json.
- [ ] The release-specific guard and workflow pin unit tests
      (tests/unit/test_release_guards.py and tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py) all pass.
- [ ] "make lint" exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [ ] "make typecheck" exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [ ] "make test" exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [ ] "python -m build" produces the 0.13.1 wheel and sdist.
- [ ] "python -m twine check" exits 0 for the built artifacts.
- [ ] The release commit contains DCO sign-off, a Gerrit Change-Id, and this rebar-ticket
      trailer.
- [ ] Gerrit records LLM-Review +1 on the release change.
- [ ] Gerrit records Verified +1 on the release change.
- [ ] Gerrit has no unresolved comments on the release change.
- [ ] Gerrit submits the release change and the resulting commit is on main.
- [ ] release.yml is dispatched from main with version input 0.13.1.
- [ ] The required pypi environment deployment is approved.
- [ ] Every required release.yml job completes successfully (build, wheel_test, sdist_test,
      publish, mcp_verify, mcp_registry, github_release).
- [ ] PyPI serves nava-rebar 0.13.1.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The pypi-attestations verifier passes against the published 0.13.1
      wheel scoped to the navapbc/rebar repository.
- [ ] [non-codebase] GitHub tag v0.13.1 resolves to the released main commit.
- [ ] [non-codebase] GitHub Release v0.13.1 is marked Latest and attaches the 0.13.1 wheel
      and sdist.
- [ ] [non-codebase, known-blocked-risk] MCP Registry reports io.github.navapbc/rebar
      version 0.13.1 as isLatest, or (if blocked by the known OAuth-App restriction even
      after the mitigation above) a linked follow-up ticket documents the gap and this item
      is explicitly marked as the accepted exception.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Homebrew tap Formula/rebar.rb points to the 0.13.1 PyPI sdist URL with
      matching SHA-256 (or the scheduled autobump run is confirmed to have picked it up).
- [ ] A fresh channel install of nava-rebar[mcp]==0.13.1 passes scripts/probe_rebar.py with
      zero failures.
- [ ] Release receipts, any exceptions, and the rollback disposition are recorded on this
      ticket.
